question: Can a straight-line Classic program (IN, then ROT/CRAZY at deterministic addresses, then OUT) compute b -> (b+1) mod 256?

L1_crazy_injective_iff_m_is_29524.statement: crazy(., m) is injective on 0..3^10-1 exactly when m == (3^10-1)/2 == 29524.
L1_crazy_injective_iff_m_is_29524.method: exhaustive: all 59049 values of m against all 59049 inputs

L3_both_generators_are_coordinate_wise.statement: For ROT and for CRAZY(.,29524), every output trit is a function of exactly one input trit.
L3_both_generators_are_coordinate_wise.method: 3006 values per generator; for each output coordinate i, every candidate input coordinate j is tested for consistency

L4_compositions_stay_coordinate_wise.statement: Compositions of ROT and CRAZY(.,29524) remain coordinate-wise, so each output trit still depends on exactly one input trit.
L4_compositions_stay_coordinate_wise.method: closure of the two generators under composition

consequence: L1 restricts any injective straight-line program to CRAZY with m=29524; L2 keeps ROT injective; L3 and L4 say every such program is coordinate-wise. Increment is not coordinate-wise: no single input trit determines output trit 0, because increment carries. Verified for all 10 candidate coordinates j.

search_evidence.straight_line_family: IN + up to 8 of {ROT,CRAZY,NOP,MOVD} + OUT + HALT: no program maps all 256 bytes to b+1
search_evidence.jmp_family_with_complete_fill: [MOVD,JMP] + up to 4 of {JMP,IN,ROT,MOVD,CRAZY,NOP} + OUT + HALT with the full 59049-cell lazy fill: no program found
search_evidence.control: IN;OUT;HALT is the identity on probe bytes 0,1,2,127,255

claim: CLASSIC_STRAIGHT_LINE_INCREMENT=IMPOSSIBLE, with machine-checked lemmas. The README row stays NOT_IMPLEMENTED and the missing ingredient is named: data-dependent control flow (computed JMP chains or loops).
not_claimed: This does not prove +1 is impossible in Classic Malbolge. It excludes one family only.
self_correction: Two earlier framings in this same session were wrong and are not used: the trit-multiset invariant (crazy swaps digits 0 and 1 per position, so counts change) and the same-index notion of trit-wise (ROT permutes positions). Both were replaced before any claim was written.
